Second, the controller uses a three-level degrade/shed mechanism to gracefully handle capacity constraints and prevent hard failures. This mechanism consists of three levels: soft degrade, medium degrade, and hard shed.

At the soft degrade level, the controller begins to gently reduce the load on the affected region by redirecting some of the traffic to nearby regions. This allows the affected region to recover from the capacity constraint without causing significant disruption to the overall system.

At the medium degrade level, if the capacity constraint persists, the controller will begin to more aggressively redirect traffic away from the affected region and towards nearby regions that have sufficient capacity to handle the additional load.

At the hard shed level, if the capacity constraint becomes severe enough to cause significant disruption to the overall system, the controller will make the decision to hard shed the affected region, which means completely removing it from the system and redirecting all of the traffic that was previously going to that region to nearby regions that have sufficient capacity to handle the additional load. This is a last resort measure that is only taken when all other measures have failed to prevent significant disruption to the overall system.
